questions.description: How are habitual running exposures associated with event performance?
questions.gap: No randomized baseline-relative dose/frequency optimization or individual marginal-benefit estimate in hybrid athletes.

questions.description: How are changes in running exposure related to running-related injury?
questions.gap: No validated individual safe progression rate, causal threshold or injury predictor.

questions.description: Do adaptive running programs improve performance relative to predefined programs?
questions.gap: Separate dose, timing, adherence and feedback contributions; no direct dual-experienced trial.

questions.description: How do endurance intensity distributions influence specific outcomes?
questions.gap: No universal optimal distribution; reconcile method, comparator and overlapping trials.

questions.description: How does quantification method change observed intensity distribution?
questions.gap: Need criterion-specific historical boundaries and aligned observations; no universal provider-zone equivalence.

questions.description: How do field-derived intensity anchors agree with reference protocols and repeat?
questions.gap: Method-specific threshold definitions, uncertainty and longitudinal responsiveness need review.

questions.description: How repeatable are standardized running performance tests?
questions.gap: No universal minimum meaningful change or unrestricted race comparability.

questions.description: What measurement properties support submaximal exercise HR as a field observation?
questions.gap: Team-sport estimates indirect; individual longitudinal fitness inference and response thresholds unvalidated.

questions.description: How do wearable aerobic-capacity estimates agree with laboratory values?
questions.gap: Individual change sensitivity, hardware and algorithm versions require validation.

questions.description: How are prolonged-running response descriptors associated with performance?
questions.gap: No causal adaptive rule or validated field decoupling threshold.

claims.assertion: Higher reported preparation mileage was associated with shorter half-marathon finish time in the adjusted model.
claims.limitations: Observational, selected finishers, self-reported exposure and residual confounding; no causal dose recommendation.
claims.assessment: Moderate descriptive relevance but weak causal directness.

support.locator: Table 3, Half marathon, Weekly training volume, >32 versus reference 20–32 km
support.restriction: Association, not an intervention; observed categories are not targets.

claims.assertion: A longer reported longest run was associated with shorter half-marathon finish time.
claims.limitations: Same cohort as mileage result; correlated training characteristics, no causal increment established.
claims.assessment: Residual confounding and self-report limit transfer.

support.locator: Table 3, Half marathon, Longest endurance run, >21 versus 15–21 km
support.restriction: Not evidence to prescribe a run exceeding race distance.

claims.assertion: Compared with the preceding longest run, higher single-session distance-change categories were associated with higher overuse injury hazard than the reference category.
claims.limitations: Self-reported outcome, observational exposure, residual/time-varying confounding; not a causal risk threshold.
claims.assessment: Large cohort, precise associations, but no intervention validation; low confidence in causal action.

support.locator: Abstract Results; Table 1; Fig. 3A; Methods exposure definition
support.restriction: Session distance relative to longest run in preceding 30 days, not weekly mileage; HRR not absolute probability.

claims.assertion: The graded program did not demonstrate lower injury incidence than the standard novice program.
claims.limitations: Different program durations, novice sample, not an equivalence test.
claims.assessment: Randomized comparison but indirect and interval not extracted.

support.result: 20.8% vs 20.3%; p=.90; confidence interval not extracted.
support.restriction: Program comparison, not isolated effect of changing weekly mileage.

claims.assertion: The 16-week injury-risk difference between the two assigned progression programs was uncertain.
claims.limitations: Large preconditioning censoring; wide interval; no claim of equivalence or performance benefit.
claims.assessment: Limited precision and indirect hybrid applicability.

support.result: Reported risk difference −14.0 percentage points (95% CI −36.9 to 8.9).
support.restriction: Confirm sign and censoring estimand against full text before approval.

claims.assertion: The individualized group improved 10-km time more than the predefined training group in the studied program.
claims.limitations: Small multicomponent comparison; allocation, attrition and dose differences require review; no isolated effect of adjusting volume or HRV.
claims.assessment: Promising direct adaptive endurance contrast, not validated hybrid policy.

support.locator: Results, 10-km running time, Fig. 3; T1 to T3
support.restriction: Six-week volume plus six-week interval periods; no transfer approved.

claims.assertion: The pooled VO2peak change favored polarized training by a small standardized effect.
claims.limitations: Mixed endurance sports/comparators; subgroup duration and training level confounded; not race performance.
claims.assessment: Author certainty high; provisional moderate for narrow pooled contrast, low for hybrid policy.

support.restriction: VO2peak only; not individual expected gain or optimum ratio.

claims.assertion: The pooled time-trial contrast did not demonstrate an advantage of polarized training.
claims.limitations: Mixed modalities and TT durations; no equivalence test; comparator heterogeneity.
claims.assessment: Interval includes effects in either direction; lower directness to running-only hybrids.

claims.assertion: The individual-participant network comparison did not establish a time-trial advantage for polarized versus pyramidal training.
claims.limitations: Mixed sports; intervals and network details outstanding; overlap with Oliveira review.

support.locator: Abstract Results, time-in-HR-zone POL versus PYR
support.result: SMD −0.05, p=.34; confidence interval not extracted.
support.restriction: Definition is HR time in zone; not session-goal allocation.

claims.assertion: The 5-km time trajectories differed across the four assigned intensity-distribution sequences.
claims.limitations: Omnibus interaction not a pairwise contrast; small groups, fast male runners; verify actual dose and attrition.
claims.assessment: Controlled study supports further sequence appraisal but does not identify optimal hybrid sequence.

support.result: Group×time F(6,112)=5.2, p=.0001; mean percent changes PYR −0.6±0.6, POL −1.1±1.1, PYR→POL −1.5±0.7, POL→PYR −0.9±0.8 (SD).
support.restriction: Descriptive means and omnibus interaction; no universal sequence conclusion.

claims.assertion: Different HR quantification methods classified the same training exposure into different intensity distributions.
claims.limitations: Small non-running sample, no intervention efficacy or universal zone boundaries.
claims.assessment: Direct descriptive method comparison; transfer limited to conceptual denominator distinction.

support.restriction: Different denominators; not evidence that either distribution is optimal.

claims.assertion: Critical speed from the studied single-visit track protocol had low reported repeat-test variability.
claims.limitations: Ten men, maximal efforts, protocol dependent; not arbitrary training-run estimates or longitudinal validity.

support.locator: Abstract Results, coefficient of variation of repeat tests
support.result: CS CV 0.4% (95% confidence limits 0.3–0.8%); D′ CV 13% (10–27%).
support.restriction: 3600/2400/1200 m protocol; estimates are model parameters, not laboratory threshold measurements.

claims.assertion: Repeat competitive outdoor 5-km tests had a reported typical finish-time error of approximately 15 seconds in this sample.
claims.limitations: 15 runners, protocol and conditions specific; not a universal minimal meaningful change.
claims.assessment: Small repeatability study; no hybrid-specific calibration.

support.restriction: Repeatability of task performance, not intervention effect.

claims.assertion: Standardized submaximal exercise HR showed a pooled typical error of 1.6 percentage points in team-sport studies.
claims.limitations: Team sports, protocol heterogeneity, no individual response calibration or physiological diagnosis.
claims.assessment: Pooled repeatability estimate, prediction interval broader; indirect runner transfer.

support.restriction: HR expressed relative to HRmax; not bpm or universal decision threshold.

claims.assertion: Exercise-based wearable estimates had small pooled mean bias but broad limits of agreement against laboratory VO2max.
claims.limitations: Devices and protocols heterogeneous, limited repeatability evidence, correction requires review.
claims.assessment: Criterion agreement not longitudinal responsiveness; individual error substantial.

support.result: Bias −0.09 mL/kg/min; pooled limits of agreement −9.92 to +9.74 mL/kg/min.
support.restriction: Limits of agreement, not CI of mean or detectable change.

claims.assertion: Runners in higher late/early decoupling groups had slower mean marathon finish times.
claims.limitations: Same-race predictor contains speed; confounding and selection; no causal or prospective adaptive validation.
claims.assessment: Large observational dataset, indirect to easy runs and shorter races.

support.locator: Methods segment definitions and abstract Results, low/moderate/high decoupling
support.result: Mean finish time 217.3±33.1, 224.9±31.7, 238.5±30.7 min; group comparisons reported p<.01.
support.restriction: 35–40 km vs 5–10 km normalized internal/external ratio; descriptive groups not cutoffs for coaching.

methods.question: running-adaptive-programming
methods.description: Review actual habitual running exposure, goals, tolerability and joint constraints before proposing hold, redistribution, increase or reduction.
methods.provenance: Research Packet 005, revision 0.1, candidate policies and periodization methodology.
methods.tradeoffs: No universal mileage rule; multicomponent intervention does not isolate dose. Maintain productive exposure; defer with unknown history or safety concern.

methods.question: running-intensity-distribution
methods.description: Choose session purpose and suitable intensity anchor; report intended and actual distribution separately with explicit denominator and method.
methods.provenance: Research Packet 005, revision 0.1, candidate policies and periodization methodology.
methods.tradeoffs: No universal ratio, no physiological zone inference from label; qualitative effort when numerical anchor insufficient.

methods.question: running-field-performance-reliability
methods.description: Assess task-specific observed performance using comparable protocol and context, report uncertainty, and distinguish estimates from reference outcomes.
methods.provenance: Research Packet 005, revision 0.1, candidate policies and periodization methodology.
methods.tradeoffs: Test burden and confounding; no universal detectable-change cutoff or causal attribution.

methods.question: running-durability-observation
methods.description: Use paired segment HR/speed only when granularity and conditions support descriptive comparison; otherwise ask about late-run tolerance.
methods.provenance: Research Packet 005, revision 0.1, candidate policies and periodization methodology.
methods.tradeoffs: No clinical or performance threshold, no progression triggered by decoupling alone.
